prompt: An ingestion task and a validation task must both finish successfully before a publish task runs. Which dependency should publish use?

options.text: Depend on both tasks with All succeeded
Depend only on ingestion with All done
Depend on validation with At least one failed
Add no dependencies and delay publish by five minutes

explanation: Task dependencies and run-if conditions define the execution graph. All succeeded requires every dependency to succeed. Other run-if conditions support recovery or partial-success flows, so successful upstream execution is not required for every possible task configuration.

prompt: A Lakeflow notebook task fails transiently and has two retries configured. What does that setting permit?

options.text: Retry attempts after the initial attempt, up to the configured limit
An unlimited number of retries for any error
Changing the source code automatically to fix validation errors
Marking the task successful without executing it again

explanation: Retry settings control additional task attempts and intervals. They can recover transient failures but do not fix deterministic data or code errors. Final job outcome also depends on downstream control flow and leaf tasks.

prompt: A downstream task needs a value computed by an upstream notebook during the same job run. What should the notebooks use?

Write the value to a local driver variable and read it in the next task
Use a job schedule parameter that is set after the run begins
Read the value from the upstream task log

explanation: dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set() and get() enable passing key-value pairs between tasks in a multi-task job. A task sets a value: dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set("key", value). Downstream tasks retrieve it: dbutils.jobs.taskValues.get("upstream_task", "key"). This enables dynamic workflows where later tasks use outputs from earlier tasks.

Use the cluster Restart button and assume all failed tasks rerun
Disable the ingestion table transaction log

explanation: Repair run re-executes failed or selected tasks within the job run recovery workflow. Successful upstream work can be preserved. Compute restart and job run repair are different operations; validate the repaired result.

To provide a SQL warehouse for interactive queries
To grant table permissions to users

explanation: Databricks Workflows is the orchestration service for scheduling and running jobs composed of tasks (notebooks, JARs, Python, SQL, Delta Live Tables). It supports task dependencies, retries, notifications, and monitoring. Workflows enables production deployment of data pipelines with reliable execution and error handling.

A single Spark task with no configuration or scheduling
A catalog object that stores table rows
A compute cluster that remains available after the job run

explanation: A job groups tasks with dependencies, parameters, and execution settings. It can be triggered manually, by a schedule, or by data events. Tasks can use supported serverless, jobs compute, or SQL warehouse options according to task type.

prompt: In Lakeflow Jobs, what is a run?

options.text: A single execution of a job with a specific start time, status, and logs
The saved job definition before execution
A permanent table created by a task
A schedule shared by every job in the workspace

explanation: A Run represents a single execution of a job. Each run has a unique run ID, start/end times, status (pending, running, succeeded, failed), and output logs. You can view run history, compare runs, and rerun specific runs. Runs enable tracking job execution history and debugging failures.

prompt: What does max_concurrent_runs control?

options.text: To control how many instances of the same job can run simultaneously
How many tasks can exist in the job definition
How many retries each task receives
How many clusters are available to all workspace users

explanation: max_concurrent_runs limits simultaneous executions of the same job. Default is 1 (only one run at a time). If a new run is triggered while another is running, it queues or skips based on configuration. This prevents resource exhaustion and conflicting operations on the same data.

A separate notebook copy for each date range
The job time zone as the only date parameter
A task timeout containing the date range

explanation: Job parameters make workload code reusable, and run-specific values can override defaults. Notebook code can read parameters through widgets; other task types have their own parameter interfaces. Configuration parameters are distinct from compute sizing.

Concatenate arbitrary user input into SQL without validation
Grant the job owner access to every table automatically
Use the parameter as a filesystem path regardless of table permissions

explanation: Use runtime parameters to reuse workload code. Validate any identifier against the intended catalog/schema or approved choices, and use the supported table reader or identifier parameterization. Parameterization does not grant access to otherwise unauthorized tables.

prompt: What does a task timeout configure?

options.text: To define the maximum time a task can run before being automatically terminated
The maximum age of the job definition
The amount of time a job waits for a schedule to start
The duration for which task logs are retained

explanation: Task timeout (in DLT and job tasks) sets the maximum duration before automatic termination. This prevents runaway tasks from consuming resources indefinitely. If timeout is reached, the task fails. Useful for: preventing hung queries, controlling costs, and ensuring SLAs are met.

prompt: A job is at its maximum concurrent runs and queuing is enabled. What happens to another eligible run?

options.text: It waits in the queue for available capacity, subject to queue limits
It permanently replaces the running job definition
It always starts concurrently despite the configured limit
It changes the maximum concurrent runs setting

explanation: Queuing lets eligible runs wait instead of being immediately skipped when capacity limits apply. Runs remain subject to queue lifetime and other platform limits. This is separate from the number of parallel tasks inside a run.

prompt: Why use a fresh classic jobs compute environment for independent job runs?

options.text: To reduce interference from state or libraries left by previous interactive sessions
To guarantee different jobs cannot write to the same Delta table
To remove the need to configure dependency versions
To make every job run immune to data quality errors

explanation: Run-scoped jobs compute reduces environmental interference from interactive use. It still needs explicit dependency configuration and data access permissions. Shared task compute within one run does not establish isolation between task code states.

options.text: To control which principals can view, trigger, or manage the orchestration resource
To grant every task automatic access to all governed data
To decide which rows a dashboard viewer can see
To select the cloud region for serverless compute

explanation: Job permissions control access to the job resource. Data access during execution is checked against the Run as identity and the relevant data privileges. Permission labels and operations follow the current job ACL model; job ownership is separate from execution identity.

prompt: Which Quartz cron expression, with the job time zone set to UTC, schedules a Lakeflow Job daily at 03:00?
explanation: Databricks advanced schedules use Quartz cron syntax with a seconds field. 0 0 3 * * ? means second 0, minute 0, hour 3, every day and month, with no specific day-of-week. Set the time zone explicitly.

Starts the job only when a Unity Catalog table changes
Runs the job only when a new file arrives
Retries a task after a task-level error

explanation: Job schedules automatically trigger job runs at defined times or intervals using cron expressions (e.g., daily at midnight, hourly). This enables automation of ETL pipelines, reports, and maintenance tasks without manual intervention. Schedules can be paused, modified, or triggered on-demand.

Creates a new job without running it

A column mask on the destination

Grant SELECT to the dashboard viewer

Disable every job dependency

An Auto Loader rescue mode

All three run without dependencies

The task should delete its checkpoint after writing
The task should change its Run as user on each attempt
